text: This king of Corinth was punished in the underworld for cheating death. He was forced to push a huge boulder up a hill, only to watch it roll back down each time it neared the top. For 10 points, name this figure whose name now describes an endless, futile task.

This god was born on the island of Delos after his mother Leto was refused shelter by most lands. He killed the serpent Python at Delphi, and he flayed the satyr Marsyas after a music contest. He drove the sun chariot in some later traditions and led the Muses. For 10 points, name this twin brother of Artemis, the Greek god of music, prophecy, and healing.

This god ruled the sky and wielded thunderbolts forged by the Cyclopes. He overthrew his father Cronus with the help of his siblings. He lived on Mount Olympus with his wife Hera. For 10 points, name this king of the Greek gods.

This goddess sprang fully grown from the forehead of her father after he swallowed her mother Metis. She competed with Poseidon to become patron of a city and gave it the olive tree. Her symbols include the owl and the aegis. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of wisdom and warfare, patron of Athens.

This god was granted rule over the sea in a three-way division of the world with his brothers. He created the first horse by striking the ground with his weapon. He carries a trident. For 10 points, name this Greek god of the sea and earthquakes.

This goddess is the wife and sister of Zeus and is often angered by his affairs. She sent snakes to attack the infant Heracles in his crib. Her sacred animal is the peacock. For 10 points, name this Greek queen of the gods and goddess of marriage.

This goddess was the twin sister of Apollo and was born on Delos. She hunts with a silver bow and is accompanied by deer. She turned the hunter Actaeon into a stag. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon.

This god was the lover of Aphrodite and was the son of Zeus and Hera. His sons Phobos and Deimos, whose names mean fear and panic, accompanied him into battle. His Roman counterpart is Mars. For 10 points, name this Greek god of war.

This goddess was born from sea foam near the island of Cyprus. She promised Paris the most beautiful woman in the world as a reward in a famous contest. Her son is Eros. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of love and beauty, called Venus by the Romans.

This god was thrown from Olympus by his mother and became lame. He built the thunderbolts of Zeus, the armor of Achilles, and a golden net that trapped his wife. For 10 points, name this Greek god of the forge and blacksmiths.

This god wears winged sandals and a winged hat and carries a staff entwined with two snakes called the caduceus. He guided souls to the underworld and delivered messages for Zeus. For 10 points, name this Greek messenger god.

This goddess was grief-stricken when her daughter was abducted, causing a famine on the earth. She taught Triptolemus the art of agriculture. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of the harvest and mother of Persephone.

This god was raised by nymphs after being born from the thigh of Zeus. He was worshipped with wild festivals and was accompanied by satyrs and maenads. Grapevines and ivy were sacred to him. For 10 points, name this Greek god of wine.

This god ruled the underworld and wore a helmet that made him invisible. He abducted Persephone to be his queen. His realm was guarded by a three-headed dog. For 10 points, name this Greek god of the dead.

This goddess ate pomegranate seeds in the underworld and so had to return there for part of every year. Her yearly return from below was said to bring spring. For 10 points, name this daughter of Demeter, queen of the underworld.

This hero was set twelve labors by King Eurystheus as punishment for killing his own family in a fit of madness. He wore the skin of the Nemean lion. For 10 points, name this strongest of the Greek heroes.

This hero killed Medusa by looking only at her reflection in a polished shield. He rescued Andromeda from a sea monster. He was born after Zeus came to his mother Danae as a shower of gold. For 10 points, name this Greek hero.
This hero navigated the Labyrinth of Crete with the help of a ball of thread from Ariadne. He was the son of King Aegeus of Athens. For 10 points, name this slayer of the Minotaur.

This hero spent ten years trying to return to Ithaca after the Trojan War. He blinded the Cyclops Polyphemus and resisted the song of the Sirens. His wife Penelope waited for him. For 10 points, name this protagonist of Homer's Odyssey.

This warrior was dipped into the River Styx by his mother Thetis, leaving only his heel vulnerable. He sulked in his tent after a quarrel with Agamemnon and later killed Hector. For 10 points, name this greatest Greek warrior of the Trojan War.
This monster had snakes for hair and turned anyone who looked at her into stone. She was one of three Gorgon sisters, though the only mortal one. For 10 points, name this monster beheaded by Perseus.

This monster had the head of a bull and the body of a man. It was kept in a maze built by Daedalus and was fed young people sent from Athens. For 10 points, name this creature of Crete, killed by Theseus.

Epimetheus ignored his brother's warning and married this woman, who was given a gift by the gods that she was told never to open. Her curiosity led her to lift the lid of a large storage jar, and sorrows and diseases escaped, leaving only hope behind. For 10 points, name this first woman of Greek myth.

This Titan stole fire from the gods and gave it to humans. As punishment, Zeus chained him to a rock where an eagle ate his liver each day. For 10 points, name this Titan whose name means forethought.

This musician played a lyre so beautifully that animals and trees followed him. He went to the underworld to retrieve his wife Eurydice but lost her when he looked back. For 10 points, name this legendary Greek poet and musician.
This king of Phrygia was granted a wish by Dionysus, and everything he touched turned to gold. He later was given donkey ears by Apollo. For 10 points, name this king with the golden touch.
This young man ignored his father's warning and flew too close to the sun with wings made of feathers and wax. The wax melted and he fell into the sea. For 10 points, name this son of Daedalus.
This winged horse sprang from the blood of Medusa when she was beheaded. It was ridden by Bellerophon when he killed the Chimera. For 10 points, name this flying horse of Greek myth.

This creature was the offspring of the monsters Typhon and Echidna. It had a serpent for a tail and was often shown as a three-headed dog. Souls could enter its master's realm but could not leave past it, and Heracles dragged it to the surface as his final labor. For 10 points, name this guardian of the underworld.

The Greeks hid warriors inside this giant wooden structure, which the Trojans dragged into their city. Odysseus is credited with the idea. For 10 points, name this construction that ended the Trojan War, a gift that was really a trick.

text: This god sacrificed one of his eyes at the well of Mimir to gain wisdom and hung himself from a tree for nine nights to learn the runes. He rides an eight-legged horse and is accompanied by two ravens and two wolves. For 10 points, name this one-eyed chief of the Norse gods.

This god is the son of Odin and wields a hammer that returns to his hand after being thrown. He rides a chariot pulled by two goats and wears a belt that doubles his strength. Thunder was said to be the sound of his chariot. For 10 points, name this red-bearded Norse god of thunder.

This trickster shape-shifting caused the death of Baldr and gave birth to the horse Sleipnir after turning into a mare. He fathered the wolf Fenrir and the world serpent with a giantess. For 10 points, name this Norse god of mischief, who is bound beneath the earth until Ragnarok.

This is the name of Thor's weapon, a short-handled hammer made by the dwarves. A giant named Thrym once stole it and demanded the goddess Freya as his bride. For 10 points, name this hammer, which Thor uses to fight giants.

Warriors who died bravely in battle were carried by Valkyries to this hall, whose roof is made of golden shields. There they feast and fight each day in preparation for the final battle. Odin presides over it. For 10 points, name this hall of the slain in Asgard.

This is the realm of the Aesir gods, connected to the world of humans by a rainbow bridge. Its halls include Valhalla and the homes of Thor and Baldr. A great wall around it was built by a giant disguised as a builder. For 10 points, name this home of the Norse gods.

This enormous ash tree connects the nine worlds of Norse cosmology. A dragon gnaws at its roots, and a squirrel runs up and down its trunk carrying insults. The gods hold their daily council beneath it. For 10 points, name this world tree.

This is the final battle in which gods and giants destroy each other, after which the world sinks into the sea and is reborn. It is foretold to follow three winters without a summer. For 10 points, name this Norse doomsday, whose name means fate of the gods.

This giant wolf, a son of Loki, was raised among the gods, but they grew afraid of his growth and chained him on an island. A prophecy says that at Ragnarok he will break free, open his jaws from earth to sky, and swallow Odin. For 10 points, name this monstrous wolf.

This goddess, the wife of Odin, knew the fates of all but never spoke of them. She asked every plant and animal to promise not to harm her son, but she overlooked the mistletoe. For 10 points, name this queen of the Norse gods and goddess of marriage.

This god was killed when his blind brother Hodr threw a mistletoe dart at him, guided by Loki. He was the brightest and most beloved of the gods. His death was one of the signs of the coming end of the world. For 10 points, name this son of Odin and Frigg.

This one-handed god of war and justice put his hand into the mouth of a wolf as a pledge of good faith. When the gods did not release the wolf, he lost the hand. For 10 points, name this Norse god who gave his name to Tuesday.

This watchman of the gods lives at the edge of heaven and can hear grass growing on the earth. He needs less sleep than a bird and will blow the Gjallarhorn to warn of the final battle. For 10 points, name this guardian of the rainbow bridge.

This is the name of the middle realm in Norse myth, home to humans. It is surrounded by an ocean in which a great serpent lies coiled. Its name means middle enclosure. For 10 points, name this world of men, between Asgard and the realm of giants.

This enormous sea serpent is a child of Loki and lies coiled around the world, biting its own tail. Thor once tried to catch it on a fishing trip, and they are fated to kill each other at Ragnarok. For 10 points, name this serpent, also called the Midgard Serpent.

This is the name of the eight-legged horse ridden by Odin. It was born when Loki, in the form of a mare, was impregnated by a stallion belonging to a giant builder. It is the fastest of all horses. For 10 points, name this steed.
This burning, three-colored bridge links Asgard to Midgard. It is guarded by Heimdall, and the sons of Muspell will break it at the end of the world. For 10 points, name this Norse rainbow bridge.

This goddess was the daughter of Loki who rules over a realm of the dishonored dead. She is described as half living and half corpse, with a face that is partly blue-black. Those who die of sickness or old age go to her. For 10 points, name this Norse goddess of the underworld.

Odin sends these two birds out each day to fly over the world and bring back news. Their names mean thought and memory. For 10 points, name this pair of ravens, who perch on the shoulders of the chief of the gods.

This Vanir god gave his magical sword to his servant Skirnir so that he could woo the giantess Gerd for him. He rides a golden boar named Gullinbursti, and he is the twin brother of Freya. For 10 points, name this Norse god of fertility, sunshine, and rain.

This goddess guards apples that keep the gods young. The giant Thiazi once kidnapped her, and the gods aged until Loki rescued her. For 10 points, name this Norse goddess of youth, the wife of the poet god Bragi.

The gods created the world from the body of this first giant, using his flesh for the earth, his blood for the seas, and his skull for the sky. He was slain by Odin and his brothers Vili and Ve. For 10 points, name this primeval frost giant.

These are the members of the main group of Norse gods, including Odin, Thor, and Baldr, who live in Asgard. They fought a war against the Vanir before the two groups made peace. For 10 points, name this group of Norse deities.

After Odin drank from his well, this being served as the keeper of wisdom beneath Yggdrasil. He was sent as a hostage to the Vanir, who beheaded him in anger, but Odin preserved the head with herbs and consulted it for counsel. For 10 points, name this wise figure.

This is the name of the yawning void that existed before creation in Norse myth. It lay between the realm of fire and the realm of ice, and where their forces met, the first giant came to be. For 10 points, name this primordial emptiness.

This weapon was made by dwarves, the sons of Ivaldi, during a contest arranged by Loki. It never misses its target, and oaths sworn on it cannot be broken. Odin hurled it over the ranks of the Vanir to begin the first war. For 10 points, name this spear of the chief Norse god.

This giantess's father was killed by the gods, so she traveled to Asgard in armor to demand compensation. She was allowed to choose a husband by seeing only his feet, and she picked a god of the sea thinking he was Baldr. For 10 points, name this winter goddess.

This sea god, the father of Freyr and Freya, was sent to live among the Aesir as a hostage. His marriage to the giantess Skadi failed because she could not bear the sea birds and he could not bear the mountains. For 10 points, name this Vanir god.

Loki cut off all of this goddess's golden hair as a prank. To avoid the anger of her husband, he swore to have dwarves forge a replacement of real gold that would grow like natural hair. For 10 points, name this wife of the thunder god.

text: This god was shown with the head of a falcon topped by a solar disk. Each night he sailed his boat through the underworld, where he fought the serpent Apep, and each morning he was reborn. Pharaohs claimed to be his sons. For 10 points, name this Egyptian sun god.

This Egyptian god was murdered and dismembered by his brother Set. His wife gathered the pieces of his body and revived him long enough to conceive a son. He then became ruler of the dead and is often shown with green skin. For 10 points, name this Egyptian god of the afterlife.

This Egyptian goddess searched the Nile Delta for the pieces of her murdered husband. She used magic to protect her infant son Horus from Set. She is often shown with a throne on her head or with wings. For 10 points, name this goddess of magic and motherhood.
This Egyptian god was shown with the head of a jackal. He supervised the mummification of the dead and weighed the hearts of the deceased against a feather. For 10 points, name this god of embalming.

This Egyptian god was a falcon-headed sky god whose eye was a symbol of protection and healing. He lost an eye in a long battle to avenge the murder of his father. The pharaoh was seen as a living form of him. For 10 points, name this son of Isis and Osiris.

This Hindu god preserves the universe and returns to earth in ten avatars, including Rama and Krishna. He is shown with blue skin, reclining on the serpent Shesha. His mount is the eagle Garuda. For 10 points, name this member of the Hindu trimurti, the preserver.

This Hindu god wears a crescent moon and a cobra, and his third eye can destroy with fire. The river Ganges falls through his hair. He is called the destroyer in the trimurti and dances the cosmic dance of Nataraja. For 10 points, name this Hindu god.

This Hindu god has the head of an elephant, and he rides a mouse. He is the remover of obstacles, and a story says he broke off his own tusk to write the Mahabharata. For 10 points, name this son of Shiva and Parvati.

This hero of Chinese myth was born from a stone egg and gained magical powers, including seventy-two transformations. He wields a staff that can change its size and rides a cloud. He accompanies the monk Tripitaka to India. For 10 points, name this Monkey King of Journey to the West.

This Egyptian god of writing and wisdom was shown with the head of an ibis. He was believed to have invented hieroglyphs, and he recorded the verdict when hearts were weighed in the underworld. His city was Hermopolis. For 10 points, name this scribe of the gods.

This Egyptian god of chaos and storms ruled the desert and was shown with the head of an unidentified animal with a curved snout. He murdered his brother Osiris and fought his nephew for the throne. For 10 points, name this god of disorder.

This feathered serpent god of the Toltecs and Aztecs was said to have created humans from the bones of earlier ages, which he sprinkled with his own blood. His rival was Tezcatlipoca. For 10 points, name this Mesoamerican god, whose name means feathered serpent.

This West African trickster takes the form of a spider. In Ashanti stories, he won all the tales in the world from the sky god by capturing a python, a leopard, and hornets. For 10 points, name this clever character who is a hero of many folktales.

This Sumerian king of Uruk was two-thirds god and one-third man. After the death of his friend, he journeyed to find the secret of immortality, only to lose a magical plant to a snake. For 10 points, name this hero of the world's oldest known epic.

This Mesopotamian goddess of love and war was known as Inanna to the Sumerians. She descended to the underworld, where she was stripped of her garments at each of seven gates. For 10 points, name this Babylonian goddess.

This monkey god, a devoted follower of Rama, leapt across the sea to find Sita. He set the city of Lanka on fire with his burning tail, and he carried an entire mountain of healing herbs. For 10 points, name this Hindu monkey deity.

This Hindu goddess is shown with black or dark blue skin, wearing a garland of skulls and with her tongue sticking out. She is a fierce form of the goddess Parvati and is often depicted dancing on Shiva. For 10 points, name this goddess of destruction and time.

This Hindu goddess of wealth and good fortune is shown sitting or standing on a lotus. She emerged from the churning of the ocean of milk and is worshipped during the festival of Diwali. For 10 points, name this wife of Vishnu.

This Hindu creator god has four faces and rides a swan. He sprang from a lotus growing from the navel of Vishnu. His wife is Saraswati. For 10 points, name this member of the Hindu trimurti, the creator.

This Polynesian demigod used a magical fishhook to pull up the Hawaiian islands from the sea. He also slowed the sun so that his mother's cloth could dry and stole fire from a bird. For 10 points, name this trickster hero of the Pacific.

This Hawaiian goddess lives in the crater of Halemaumau at Kilauea. She is said to be jealous and quick to anger, and visitors who take lava rocks from the islands are believed to suffer her curse. For 10 points, name this goddess of volcanoes.

This Irish hero of the Ulster Cycle was born as Setanta but took a new name after killing a guard dog. He wielded the spear Gae Bulg and held off the armies of Queen Medb alone. For 10 points, name this Hound of Ulster.

This trickster of many Native American traditions is both a creator and a fool. In some stories he steals fire or brings death into the world by bad judgment. For 10 points, name this canine character of the American Southwest and plains.

This Aztec god was born fully armed from his mother Coatlicue and killed his sister Coyolxauhqui. He demanded human sacrifices to keep the sun moving, and his shrine was at the top of the Great Temple of Tenochtitlan. For 10 points, name this war god whose name means blue hummingbird on the left.

This primordial saltwater goddess in Babylonian myth was a chaos monster who took the form of a dragon. A storm god split her body in two to form the heavens and the earth. For 10 points, name this mother of the first gods in the Enuma Elish, killed by Marduk.

This wild man was created by the gods from clay to be a rival to a king. He lived among animals until a woman named Shamhat civilized him, and he later helped slay Humbaba. For 10 points, name this friend of Gilgamesh.

This Chinese giant was born inside a cosmic egg. He separated earth from sky by growing taller for eighteen thousand years, and after his death his body became the mountains and rivers. For 10 points, name this first being of Chinese creation myth.

This Irish hero of the Fenian Cycle gained wisdom by tasting a salmon he was cooking. He led a band of warriors called the Fianna and is said to have built a causeway to Scotland to fight a rival giant. For 10 points, name this mythical hunter-warrior, also called Fionn mac Cumhaill.

This Japanese god was the male creator who, with his wife, formed the islands from a jeweled spear dipped in the sea. After fleeing the land of the dead, he washed in a river, and from his face were born Amaterasu, the moon god, and a storm god. For 10 points, name this Shinto creator god.

text: This philosopher claimed that his wisdom consisted only in knowing that he knew nothing. He compared himself to a gadfly stinging the sleepy city of Athens and said that the unexamined life is not worth living. He left no writings of his own. For 10 points, name this teacher of Plato.

This philosopher described a realm of perfect Forms of which the physical world is only a shadow. He wrote dialogues in which his teacher is the main speaker, including the Symposium and the Phaedo. His most famous student was Aristotle. For 10 points, name this Greek philosopher.

This philosopher analyzed four kinds of causes, including the material and the final cause, and he wrote on logic, ethics, politics, and biology. He tutored the young Alexander of Macedon. Raphael painted him gesturing toward the earth in The School of Athens. For 10 points, name this student of Plato.

This is the poison, made from a plant in the parsley family, that Athens gave to condemned prisoners. A famous philosopher drank a cup of it in 399 BC after being convicted of impiety, as told in the Phaedo. For 10 points, name this poison.

This work of Plato imagines a city ruled by philosopher-kings and argues that justice is harmony among the parts of the soul and city. It begins at the house of Cephalus and features a debate with Thrasymachus. For 10 points, name this dialogue about justice, an enormous work of political philosophy.

In this allegory, prisoners are chained in an underground chamber and see only shadows cast on a wall by a fire. One prisoner escapes, is dazzled by the sun, and returns to tell others what he saw. For 10 points, name this allegory from Plato's Republic that illustrates his theory of knowledge.

This Milesian is often called the first philosopher in the Western tradition. He argued that everything is made of water and is said to have predicted a solar eclipse. For 10 points, name this Greek thinker, the first of the Seven Sages.

This Greek philosopher and mathematician founded a religious brotherhood in southern Italy that believed in reincarnation. He is famous for a theorem about right triangles and said that all things are numbers. For 10 points, name this Greek thinker.

This Greek philosopher is said to have lived in a large ceramic jar and walked around in daylight with a lamp searching for an honest man. When Alexander the Great offered him a favor, he asked the king to step out of his sunlight. For 10 points, name this Cynic.

This Roman emperor wrote a private journal of reflections while on military campaign in central Europe. Written in Greek, those Meditations advise accepting what cannot be controlled. He is the last of the Five Good Emperors. For 10 points, name this Stoic emperor.

This philosopher argued that the world is in constant flux, saying that you cannot step into the same river twice. He believed that fire is the fundamental substance and that the logos governs all change. For 10 points, name this Ephesian known as the Obscure.

This philosopher developed atomism, arguing that all matter consists of tiny indivisible particles moving in a void. His teacher was Leucippus, and he was nicknamed the Laughing Philosopher. For 10 points, name this thinker from Abdera.

This philosopher taught that pleasure is the highest good, but defined it mainly as freedom from pain and disturbance. He gathered followers in a garden in Athens and argued that death is nothing to us. For 10 points, name this founder of a school of philosophy.

This former slave and lame philosopher taught that we should focus only on what is up to us. His lectures were recorded by his student Arrian as the Discourses and the Enchiridion. For 10 points, name this Stoic of Hierapolis.

This Roman philosopher served as tutor to the emperor Nero and wrote Letters to Lucilius and On the Shortness of Life. He was ordered to take his own life in 65 AD. For 10 points, name this Stoic and playwright.

This school was founded by Plato in a grove outside Athens and lasted for centuries. Aristotle studied there for about twenty years. For 10 points, name this first institution of higher learning in the Western world.
This school in Athens was founded by Aristotle in a grove sacred to Apollo. Its members were nicknamed peripatetics because they discussed ideas while walking. For 10 points, name this school.

This work by Aristotle examines the best life for human beings and argues that virtue is a mean between excess and deficiency. It is named for his father or his son. For 10 points, name this treatise on ethics.

This school of thought took its name from a painted porch in Athens. It taught that virtue is the only good and that one should accept fate calmly. For 10 points, name this school followed by Epictetus and Marcus Aurelius.

This Greek school took its name from the word for dog. Its followers rejected wealth, fame, and social conventions in favor of living according to nature. Antisthenes is considered its founder. For 10 points, name this philosophy, associated with Diogenes.

This method of teaching involves asking a series of probing questions in order to expose contradictions in a person's beliefs. It is named for an Athenian philosopher and is often used in law schools. For 10 points, name this question-and-answer method.

This type of reasoning, studied by Aristotle, draws a conclusion from two premises, such as all men are mortal, Socrates is a man, so Socrates is mortal. For 10 points, name this form of deductive argument.

This Greek word, usually translated as flourishing or happiness, is for Aristotle the highest aim of human life. It comes from words meaning good and spirit. For 10 points, name this concept central to Greek ethics.

These were itinerant teachers in classical Greece who charged fees to teach rhetoric and the art of persuasion. Plato criticized them for treating truth as relative. Gorgias and Protagoras belonged to this group. For 10 points, name these paid teachers.

This philosopher from Elea wrote a poem in which a goddess describes the way of truth and the way of opinion. He argued that what exists is one, unchanging, and eternal, and that change is an illusion. For 10 points, name this Eleatic thinker, whose student Zeno defended his ideas.
This student of Parmenides argued that motion is impossible through paradoxes. In one, a swift runner can never overtake a slow tortoise. For 10 points, name this Eleatic philosopher.

This Milesian philosopher proposed that the origin of all things is an infinite, indefinite substance. He is credited with creating an early map of the known world. For 10 points, name this student of Thales, who named that substance the apeiron.

This philosopher, said to have accompanied Alexander the Great to India, founded a school that taught suspension of judgment as the path to peace of mind. For 10 points, name this founder of Skepticism, called Pyrrhonism after him.

This Sophist from Abdera was a friend of the statesman Pericles. He claimed that man is the measure of all things, a statement taken to mean that truth is relative to the individual. For 10 points, name this Greek thinker, the namesake of a Platonic dialogue.

This philosopher, born in Roman Egypt, taught in Rome and believed that all things emanate from a single ineffable source called the One. His student Porphyry edited his writings into the Enneads. For 10 points, name this founder of Neoplatonism.

text: This philosopher imagined an evil demon who deceives him about everything and concluded that his own existence cannot be doubted because he is thinking. He argued that mind and body are separate substances. His Discourse on Method begins with systematic doubt. For 10 points, name this French author of Meditations on First Philosophy, who said "I think, therefore I am."

This English philosopher argued that people have natural rights to life, liberty, and property and that governments exist only by the consent of the governed. His Two Treatises of Government influenced Thomas Jefferson. For 10 points, name this author of An Essay Concerning Human Understanding.

This philosopher from Konigsberg argued that we can know only the world as it appears to us and never things as they are in themselves. His major works include the Critique of Pure Reason and the Critique of Practical Reason. For 10 points, name this German Enlightenment thinker.

This German philosopher declared that God is dead and called for the coming of the Übermensch. He also wrote Thus Spoke Zarathustra and Beyond Good and Evil. His idea of the will to power opposed traditional Christian morality. For 10 points, name this philosopher.

This German philosopher and economist argued that history is driven by class struggle and that capitalism would be replaced by communism. He wrote Das Kapital while living in London. For 10 points, name this author, with Friedrich Engels, of The Communist Manifesto.

This Swiss-born philosopher argued that humans are naturally good but are corrupted by society. He began a famous book with the line that man is born free, but everywhere he is in chains. He also wrote Emile. For 10 points, name this French Enlightenment thinker, author of The Social Contract.

This French Enlightenment writer championed religious tolerance and freedom of speech, and he wrote the satire Candide. He was exiled to England and spent his last years at Ferney. For 10 points, name this author, whose real name was Francois-Marie Arouet.

This English philosopher and statesman wrote the Novum Organum, which advocated gathering evidence through experiment and induction. He is credited with the saying that knowledge is power, and he served as Lord Chancellor. For 10 points, name this father of the scientific method and author of New Atlantis.

This French philosopher wrote Being and Nothingness and the play No Exit, which includes the line that hell is other people. He argued that existence precedes essence. He refused the Nobel Prize in Literature. For 10 points, name this French existentialist.

This moral theory holds that an action is right if it produces the greatest good for the greatest number of people. It was developed by Jeremy Bentham and refined by John Stuart Mill. For 10 points, name this consequentialist philosophy.

This English philosopher wrote that without a strong government, life in the state of nature would be solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short. He lived through the English Civil War and defended absolute monarchy. For 10 points, name this author of Leviathan.

This Scottish philosopher argued that we have no rational basis for believing in cause and effect, only habit. His Treatise of Human Nature claimed that the self is a bundle of perceptions. He awoke Kant from his dogmatic slumber. For 10 points, name this skeptical empiricist.

This English philosopher wrote On Liberty, which argued that society may limit individual freedom only to prevent harm to others. He also wrote The Subjection of Women, in collaboration with Harriet Taylor. For 10 points, name this utilitarian who wrote Utilitarianism.

This English philosopher designed a circular prison called the Panopticon and requested that his preserved body be displayed after death. He wrote An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation, which measured actions by pleasure and pain. For 10 points, name this founder of modern utilitarianism.

This Danish philosopher wrote Fear and Trembling, which discusses Abraham's near-sacrifice of Isaac, and introduced the idea of the leap of faith. He published many works under pseudonyms and broke off his engagement to Regine Olsen. For 10 points, name this father of existentialism.

This German philosopher wrote the Phenomenology of Spirit and argued that history advances through a dialectical process toward freedom. He taught at the University of Berlin, and his ideas strongly influenced Marx. For 10 points, name this absolute idealist.

This French philosopher wrote The Second Sex, which says that one is not born but rather becomes a woman. She was a lifelong partner of Jean-Paul Sartre. For 10 points, name this founder of modern feminist philosophy.

This Algerian-born French writer argued in The Myth of Sisyphus that life is absurd and that one must imagine Sisyphus happy. He also wrote the novels The Stranger and The Plague. For 10 points, name this winner of the 1957 Nobel Prize in Literature.

This English philosopher wrote A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, arguing that women should receive an education equal to men. She was the mother of the author of Frankenstein. For 10 points, name this early feminist thinker.

This movement, associated with Kierkegaard, Sartre, and Camus, emphasizes individual freedom, choice, and responsibility in a world without given meaning. For 10 points, name this philosophical movement.

This principle states that one should act only according to a maxim that one could will to become a universal law. It was proposed in the Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals by a German philosopher. For 10 points, name this ethical principle.

This Latin phrase, meaning blank slate, describes the idea that the mind at birth has no innate ideas and is filled by experience. An English empiricist popularized it. For 10 points, name this phrase.

This 1651 work begins with a frontispiece showing a giant crowned figure made up of many tiny people. It argues that people give up some freedom to a sovereign in exchange for protection from violence. For 10 points, name this work named for a biblical sea monster.

This theory in philosophy holds that all knowledge comes from sensory experience rather than from innate ideas. It is usually contrasted with rationalism and is associated with British thinkers. For 10 points, name this theory of knowledge.

This Irish bishop argued that material objects exist only as perceptions in minds, summing up his position as to be is to be perceived. His Treatise concerning the Principles of Human Knowledge defended this immaterialism. For 10 points, name this philosopher, the namesake of a California city.

This Dutch philosopher was excommunicated from his Jewish community in Amsterdam and earned a living grinding lenses. His Ethics is written in the form of geometric proofs and identifies God with nature. For 10 points, name this rationalist.

This German rationalist argued that the universe is made up of simple, windowless units called monads. He claimed that we live in the best of all possible worlds and is credited with independently inventing calculus. For 10 points, name this philosopher.

This French baron wrote Persian Letters and The Spirit of the Laws, in which he argued that governmental power should be divided among separate branches. His ideas deeply influenced the framers of the United States Constitution. For 10 points, name this political philosopher.

This German pessimist argued that the world is driven by a blind, striving force he called the will. His main work, The World as Will and Representation, influenced Nietzsche and Wagner. For 10 points, name this philosopher.

This French mathematician and philosopher argued that it is rational to bet on the existence of God. He wrote the Pensees and the Provincial Letters and invented an early mechanical calculator. For 10 points, name this man who has a law of fluid pressure and a triangle named after him.

text: According to the Gospels of Matthew and Luke, Jesus was born in this town near Jerusalem, where shepherds came to see the baby. Wise men from the East are said to have followed a star to this place. Joseph and Mary traveled here for a census. For 10 points, name this town in the West Bank known as the birthplace of Jesus.

On this holiday, many Christians exchange gifts and attend church services featuring carols and nativity scenes. Decorated evergreen trees and Advent wreaths are common symbols of its season. Churches often hold a candlelit midnight service on its eve. For 10 points, name this holiday celebrated on December 25 that marks the birth of Jesus.

This Sunday begins Holy Week and recalls the day Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a donkey while crowds laid down branches and cloaks. Churches often hand out woven fronds on this day. It falls one week before Easter. For 10 points, name this Sunday named for the branches waved by the crowd.

This holiday, held fifty days after Easter, commemorates the descent of the Holy Spirit on the apostles. The Book of Acts says they were gathered together when tongues of fire appeared above them and they began to speak in other languages. Some call it the birthday of the Church. For 10 points, name this feast whose name comes from the Greek for fiftieth.

Many Christians give up a favorite food or habit during this forty-day period of fasting and prayer before Easter. It echoes the forty days Jesus spent in the wilderness. It begins on Ash Wednesday and ends before Holy Week. For 10 points, name this season of repentance and preparation before Easter.

On this day, Christians receive a cross of ashes on the forehead as a sign of repentance. Priests often say the words remember that you are dust, and to dust you shall return. It is the first day of a forty-day season of preparation. For 10 points, name this Wednesday that begins Lent.

This man was a Pharisee who persecuted early Christians until a vision of Jesus blinded him on the road to Damascus. He then made missionary journeys around the Mediterranean. Thirteen letters in the New Testament are traditionally attributed to him. For 10 points, name this apostle to the Gentiles, formerly called Saul.

This disciple is said to have betrayed Jesus to the authorities for thirty pieces of silver. He identified Jesus by greeting him with a kiss in the Garden of Gethsemane. Later he is said to have died by hanging himself. For 10 points, name this apostle whose last name probably refers to a place or group, and whose name has become a synonym for traitor.

Leonardo da Vinci painted a famous mural of this event in the refectory of a Milan monastery. Jesus is shown seated at a long table with his twelve disciples, just after saying that one of them would betray him. During this meal Jesus shared bread and wine, which is the origin of a Christian ritual. For 10 points, name this final meal before the Crucifixion.
alternates: final meal of Jesus before crucifixion

text: Jesus was baptized by John in this river, and the Gospels say the Holy Spirit descended like a dove. Today, many churches use water to perform a ritual in which a person is welcomed into the faith, either by sprinkling or by immersion. For 10 points, name this Christian sacrament of initiation that uses water.

In this Christian rite, believers eat consecrated bread and drink wine or grape juice to remember the sacrifice of Jesus. Catholics believe the elements become the body and blood of Christ, a doctrine called transubstantiation. It is also known as the Eucharist or the Lord's Supper. For 10 points, name this sacrament, a word that also means sharing in something together.

Christians who profess this doctrine believe that God exists as three persons in one being. The Nicene Creed lays it out, and the shamrock is sometimes used as a teaching symbol for it. Its three persons are the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. For 10 points, name this central Christian doctrine of the three-in-one God.

This is the last book of the Christian Bible. Its author, named John, writes of visions that include four horsemen, seven seals, a great beast, and a new heaven and new earth. It is full of symbolic imagery and is sometimes called the Apocalypse. For 10 points, name this final book of the New Testament.

Many of these 150 poems are traditionally credited to King David. One of them begins The Lord is my shepherd, and they are used as hymns and prayers in both Jewish and Christian worship. For 10 points, name this book of the Old Testament that is a collection of sacred songs and poems.

In a parable told by Jesus, a traveler is beaten by robbers and left by the road. A priest and a Levite pass him by, but a man from a region despised by the traveler's people stops to bandage his wounds and pay for his care. For 10 points, name this parable whose title now describes a person who helps strangers in need.

In a parable from the Gospel of Luke, a younger son demands his inheritance, leaves home, and wastes it all on reckless living. When famine strikes, he returns home, expecting to be punished. Instead, his father throws a feast and the older brother complains. For 10 points, name this parable about forgiveness and a returning child.

Christians recite this prayer, which Jesus taught his disciples, beginning with the words Our Father, who art in heaven. It includes the lines give us this day our daily bread and forgive us our trespasses. For 10 points, name this most widely used Christian prayer.

In this speech, delivered from a hillside in Galilee, Jesus says blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth. It begins with the Beatitudes and includes teachings such as turning the other cheek and loving your enemies. For 10 points, name this famous discourse found in the Gospel of Matthew.

Legend says this man used a three-leaf plant to explain the Trinity and drove snakes out of Ireland. Born in Roman Britain, he was captured by raiders as a teenager and later returned to Ireland as a missionary. For 10 points, name this patron saint of Ireland, whose feast day is March 17.

This Italian man gave up the wealth of his merchant father to live in poverty. He is said to have preached to birds and tamed a wolf in the town of Gubbio. He founded an order of friars, and many people ask for his blessing on animals. For 10 points, name this saint from Assisi.

This French teenager said she heard the voices of saints telling her to help the crown prince reach the throne. She led an army to lift the siege of Orleans during the Hundred Years War. She was captured, tried for heresy, and burned at the stake in 1431. For 10 points, name this saint, known as the Maid of Orleans.

This Catholic nun, born in what is now North Macedonia, founded the Missionaries of Charity in Calcutta, India. She spent decades caring for the poor, sick, and dying, and she won the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize. She was canonized as a saint in 2016. For 10 points, name this nun known for her service to the poor.

This 16th-century movement began when Martin Luther posted his Ninety-five Theses. It split Western Christianity and led to the founding of Lutheran, Reformed, and Anglican churches. John Calvin and Huldrych Zwingli were also leaders. For 10 points, name this religious upheaval that created Protestantism.

This independent city-state located inside Rome is the smallest country in the world by area. It is home to Saint Peter's Basilica, the Sistine Chapel, and the Pope. For 10 points, name this tiny nation that is the center of the Roman Catholic Church.

Pope Urban II launched the first of these medieval military campaigns in 1095 with a speech at Clermont. Christian armies from Europe sought to capture Jerusalem and other holy sites from Muslim rulers. Richard the Lionheart and Saladin met during the Third of these campaigns. For 10 points, name these religious wars of the Middle Ages.

This season of the Christian calendar begins about four weeks before Christmas. Families often light candles on a wreath, one each Sunday, and open small doors on a calendar that counts down the days. The word comes from the Latin for coming. For 10 points, name this season of waiting before Christmas.

On January 6, many Christians celebrate this feast, which commemorates the visit of the Magi to the infant Jesus. Some churches observe it as the end of the twelve days of Christmas. Its name comes from a Greek word meaning manifestation. For 10 points, name this feast, also called Three Kings Day.

The Gospel of Luke says this archangel appeared to Mary to announce that she would bear a son named Jesus. In the Book of Daniel this angel also explains visions to the prophet. In Islam, the same being brought revelations to Muhammad. For 10 points, name this messenger angel often shown holding a trumpet.

This prophet baptized people in the Jordan River and preached repentance. He wore clothes of camel hair, and his diet was locusts and wild honey. He baptized Jesus and was later beheaded at the request of Salome. For 10 points, name this cousin of Jesus.

This day of the Christian calendar remembers the crucifixion of Jesus. Churches often hold solemn services, and many Christians fast or follow the Stations of the Cross. It falls two days before Easter Sunday. For 10 points, name this Friday of Holy Week.

text: This word names the first five books of the Hebrew Bible, which are traditionally credited to Moses. A handwritten scroll of these books is kept in the ark of a synagogue and read aloud in weekly portions. The readers use a pointer called a yad. For 10 points, name this sacred text, whose name means teaching or law.

This prophet was found as a baby in a basket among the reeds of the Nile. He confronted the pharaoh with ten plagues, led the Israelites out of Egypt, and received the law on Mount Sinai. For 10 points, name this Hebrew leader who is credited as the author of the Torah.

At a seder on this holiday, families retell the story of the exodus from Egypt using a book called the Haggadah. They eat matzah, bitter herbs, and charoset, and they drink four cups of wine. For 10 points, name this eight-day spring festival of freedom from slavery.

This winter festival commemorates the rededication of the Temple in Jerusalem after the Maccabean revolt. Jewish families light one more candle each night on a special candelabrum and play with a spinning top called a dreidel. For 10 points, name this holiday also called the Festival of Lights.

This is the holiest day of the Jewish year, a day of fasting, prayer, and repentance. It falls ten days after Rosh Hashanah, and the services end with the sounding of a ram's horn. For 10 points, name this Day of Atonement.

This holiday opens the Jewish High Holy Days. It is the Jewish New Year and is celebrated with the blowing of the shofar and with apples dipped in honey to symbolize a sweet year. For 10 points, name this holiday that falls in early autumn and whose name means head of the year.

Jews observe this day of rest from Friday evening until Saturday night. Families light candles, say a blessing over wine, and eat braided bread called challah. Observant Jews avoid work on this day, as the Ten Commandments instruct. For 10 points, name this weekly holy day.

This building is the Jewish place of worship, where services are held and the Torah is read. It also serves as a place of study and community gathering. A cantor often leads the singing, and a rabbi often leads the congregation. For 10 points, name this house of prayer that is the Jewish counterpart of a church.

This title is given to a teacher and spiritual leader of a Jewish community. Such a person interprets Jewish law, leads services, and counsels congregants. The word means my master in Hebrew. For 10 points, name this position held by the leader of a synagogue.

This six-pointed shape of two overlapping triangles appears on the flag of Israel. It is also known by the name of a Hebrew king, and Nazi Germany forced Jews to wear it as a badge. For 10 points, name this symbol of Judaism.

This candelabrum with seven branches was used in the Temple in Jerusalem and is a symbol of Judaism. A version with nine branches is lit during Hanukkah. The emblem of the state of Israel includes this object. For 10 points, name this lamp stand.

This collection of rabbinic discussions of Jewish law and tradition includes the Mishnah and the Gemara. There are two versions, one compiled in Babylonia and one in the Land of Israel. For 10 points, name this central text of rabbinic Judaism, whose name means study.

God commands this man to leave his home in Ur and promises him descendants as numerous as the stars. He is told to sacrifice his son Isaac, but an angel stops him. He is a father of both Judaism and Islam. For 10 points, name this first of the three patriarchs.

According to Genesis, God told this man to build an ark to save his family and pairs of animals from a great flood. A dove returned to him with an olive branch. For 10 points, name this biblical figure whose sons were Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

Moses received these laws on two stone tablets on Mount Sinai. They include rules against murder, theft, and lying, and they require keeping the Sabbath holy. For 10 points, name these ten rules given by God to the Israelites.

The second book of the Bible tells how the Israelites were enslaved in Egypt and then freed. It includes the burning bush, the ten plagues, and the parting of the Red Sea. For 10 points, name this book, whose name means going out.

As a boy, this man defeated the giant Goliath with a sling and a stone. He later became the second king of Israel, captured Jerusalem, and is credited with writing many psalms. For 10 points, name this king, whose name is on a six-pointed star.

The Bible says this king of Israel asked God for wisdom rather than riches. He is known for settling a dispute between two women who claimed the same baby, and for building the First Temple in Jerusalem. For 10 points, name this son of David.

This holiday celebrates the rescue of the Jews of Persia from the plot of the villain Haman. People read from a scroll, dress in costumes, give gifts of food, and make noise with groggers whenever Haman is named. For 10 points, name this joyous spring holiday.

This prophet was swallowed by a great fish after trying to flee from God's command to preach in Nineveh. He spent three days in its belly before being spit out onto dry land. For 10 points, name this biblical figure.

This prophet was thrown into a den of lions after he continued to pray to God despite a royal decree. He also interpreted dreams for Babylonian kings and read the writing on the wall at Belshazzar's feast. For 10 points, name this Hebrew prophet.

At age thirteen, a Jewish boy takes on the responsibilities of adulthood in this ceremony. He reads from the Torah in front of the congregation and often celebrates with a large party. The comparable ceremony for girls is called a bat mitzvah. For 10 points, name this coming-of-age ritual.

Jewish dietary laws, called by this word, forbid eating pork and shellfish and mixing meat with dairy. Food that follows these rules is considered fit to eat. For 10 points, give this word that describes food prepared in accordance with Jewish law.

On this fall holiday, Jews build temporary huts with roofs made of branches and eat meals inside them. The huts recall the shelters the Israelites used while wandering in the desert. Observers also wave a palm branch, myrtle, willow, and a citron. For 10 points, name this festival of booths.

This word is an acronym of the three sections of the Hebrew Bible: Torah, Nevi'im, and Ketuvim. It contains the same books that Christians call the Old Testament, though arranged differently. For 10 points, name this Jewish scripture.

This surviving retaining wall of the Second Temple complex in Jerusalem is the holiest place where Jews may pray. People tuck written prayers into its cracks. It is also called the Wailing Wall. For 10 points, name this ancient limestone wall.

Esau sold his birthright to this man for a bowl of stew. He later dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven and wrestled with an angel, after which he was given the name Israel. For 10 points, name this son of Isaac whose twelve sons founded the tribes of Israel.

His brothers sold this son of Jacob into slavery out of jealousy over his colorful coat. He rose to power in Egypt after interpreting the dreams of the pharaoh. For 10 points, name this biblical figure whose story is told at the end of Genesis.

This judge of Israel was famed for his great strength, which was linked to his uncut hair. Delilah betrayed him to the Philistines, and in the end he pulled down the pillars of a temple. For 10 points, name this biblical strongman.

This ram's horn is blown on Rosh Hashanah and at the end of Yom Kippur. The Bible says its sound was heard at Mount Sinai. It produces calls named tekiah, shevarim, and teruah. For 10 points, name this ancient instrument.

text: Muslims believe this book was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad by the angel Gabriel over about twenty-three years. It is divided into 114 chapters called surahs, and it is recited in Arabic. Many Muslims memorize it in full. For 10 points, name this holy book of Islam.

This man received his first revelation in the Cave of Hira at about age forty. He preached in his hometown of Mecca, was forced to leave, and later returned in triumph. Muslims consider him the last prophet and add the phrase peace be upon him after his name. For 10 points, name this founder of Islam.

Muslims around the world face this city when they pray, and it is the destination of the annual pilgrimage. It is located in Saudi Arabia and is the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad. Non-Muslims are not allowed to enter its sacred area. For 10 points, name this holiest city of Islam.

The Prophet Muhammad moved to this city in 622 after being persecuted in Mecca. It became the capital of the first Muslim community, and the Prophet is buried here under the Green Dome. For 10 points, name this second holiest city in Islam, located in Saudi Arabia.

During this ninth month of the Islamic calendar, Muslims fast from dawn to sunset. Families gather to break the fast each evening with a meal called iftar, and many attend special night prayers. For 10 points, name this holy month of fasting that ends with Eid al-Fitr.

This holiday marks the end of Ramadan. Muslims gather for a special prayer, give charity, wear new clothes, and share sweets with family and friends. Its name means festival of breaking the fast. For 10 points, name this three-day celebration.

This holiday honors the willingness of Ibrahim to sacrifice his son at God's command. Muslims often sacrifice an animal and share the meat with the poor. It falls during the pilgrimage to Mecca. For 10 points, name this festival of sacrifice, which comes about two months after the other Eid.

Every able Muslim who can afford it is expected to make this journey to Mecca at least once. Pilgrims wear simple white clothing, walk around the Kaaba, and stand on the plain of Arafat. For 10 points, name this pilgrimage that is the fifth pillar of Islam.

This cube-shaped building draped in a black cloth sits at the center of the Great Mosque of Mecca. Muslims believe it was built by Abraham and his son Ishmael. Pilgrims walk around it seven times. For 10 points, name this holiest shrine in Islam toward which Muslims face when they pray.

Muslims gather in this building for communal prayers, especially on Fridays. It has a prayer hall, a washing area for ritual purification, and a niche pointing toward Mecca. For 10 points, name this Islamic house of worship.

The call to prayer is traditionally given from the top of this tall, slender tower attached to a mosque. Some of these towers are very ornate, and a mosque may have several. For 10 points, name this architectural feature of mosques.

This word is the title for the person who leads prayers in a mosque. It also names a leader of the Muslim community, and Shia Muslims use it for a line of spiritual successors to Muhammad. For 10 points, give this term for a prayer leader.

The first pillar of Islam is this declaration of faith. It states that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the messenger of God. Saying it with sincerity makes someone a Muslim. For 10 points, name this Islamic creed.

This is one of the five pillars of Islam, a form of required almsgiving. Muslims who are able to pay donate a set portion of their savings each year to the poor. For 10 points, name this Islamic obligation that means purification.

This branch of Islam, whose name refers to the Prophet's example, makes up the large majority of Muslims worldwide. It holds that the community chose Abu Bakr as the first caliph. For 10 points, name this branch that is the larger of the two main branches of Islam.

The followers of this branch of Islam believe Muhammad's cousin and son-in-law Ali was his rightful successor. Their name comes from a phrase meaning party of Ali. Iran and Iraq have large populations of this branch. For 10 points, name this second-largest branch of Islam.

The Islamic calendar begins with this event in 622, when Muhammad and his followers traveled from Mecca to Medina. The word means migration. For 10 points, name this journey that marks year one of the Islamic calendar.

This word names the collected sayings and actions of the Prophet Muhammad as recorded by his companions. Muslims use it, along with the Quran, as a source of guidance. For 10 points, give this term for such a reported tradition.

This term refers to the body of Islamic law, derived from the Quran, the Hadith, and scholarly reasoning. It guides worship, family matters, and many other areas of life. For 10 points, name this religious law of Islam, whose name means the path.

After Muhammad died, this word came to be used for the successor who led the Muslim community. Four of them are called the rightly guided ones. For 10 points, give this title of the political and religious head of the Islamic state, translated as successor.

This close friend of Muhammad and father of his wife Aisha became the first caliph in 632. He put down rebellions in Arabia and had the Quran gathered into written form. For 10 points, name this first of the rightly guided caliphs.
This cousin and son-in-law of Muhammad was the fourth caliph. Shia Muslims regard him as the first imam. He was the husband of Fatima and father of Hasan and Husayn. For 10 points, name this man.

This wealthy merchant of Mecca became the first wife of Muhammad. She supported him after his first revelation and was the first person to accept his message. For 10 points, name this woman, who was the mother of Fatima.

This Muslim sultan of Egypt and Syria recaptured Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187. He was known for his chivalry and was respected by Richard the Lionheart. For 10 points, name this Kurdish leader.

This symbol of a curved moon and a star appears on the flags of several Muslim-majority countries, such as Turkey and Pakistan. It is widely used to represent Islam, although it is not a religious symbol from the time of the Prophet. For 10 points, name this moon shape.

Under Islamic dietary laws, food that is permitted is described by this Arabic term, which means lawful. Pork and alcohol are forbidden. For 10 points, give this term, used to describe meat slaughtered in the prescribed way.
This person stands in a minaret or inside a mosque and calls Muslims to prayer five times a day. Bilal, a freed slave, was the first to do it. For 10 points, name this role, whose call is the adhan.
This Arabic word refers to the direction of the Kaaba in Mecca, which Muslims face when praying. A niche called the mihrab in a mosque shows it. For 10 points, name this direction of prayer.

Muslims believe the Quran was first revealed to Muhammad on this Night of Power during Ramadan. It is said to be better than a thousand months. Many Muslims spend it in prayer. For 10 points, name this night, which falls on one of the last odd nights of Ramadan.

This golden-domed shrine in Jerusalem was completed in 691 under the caliph Abd al-Malik. It stands on the Temple Mount and encloses a sacred rock from which Muslims believe Muhammad ascended to heaven. For 10 points, name this Islamic monument.

text: This prince was born in Lumbini, in what is now Nepal, and grew up in a palace shielded from suffering. After seeing an old man, a sick man, and a corpse, he gave up his wealth to seek enlightenment. He attained it beneath a fig tree after long meditation. For 10 points, name this founder of Buddhism, known by a title meaning the awakened one.

Families celebrate this autumn festival of lights by setting out small oil lamps called diyas and lighting fireworks. It honors the goddess Lakshmi and celebrates the victory of light over darkness. Many Hindus, Sikhs, and Jains observe it. For 10 points, name this holiday also known as the Festival of Lights in India.

During this spring festival, participants throw colored powder and water at each other in streets and parks. It marks the arrival of spring and celebrates the triumph of good over evil. For 10 points, name this Hindu festival of colors.

This Hindu god is the preserver in the trimurti, along with Brahma and Shiva. He is said to have come to earth in ten avatars, including Rama and Krishna. He is often shown with blue skin, resting on a serpent. For 10 points, name this deity.

This Hindu god is called the destroyer and is often shown with a third eye, a trident, and a cobra around his neck. The Ganges is said to flow from his hair. For 10 points, name this deity whose dance of destruction and creation is shown in the Nataraja form.

This Hindu god has the head of an elephant and is worshiped as the remover of obstacles. He is the son of Shiva and Parvati, and he is often depicted with a broken tusk and a mouse. For 10 points, name this deity honored at the start of new ventures.

This blue-skinned Hindu deity is the eighth avatar of Vishnu. He is known for playing the flute, stealing butter as a child, and serving as the charioteer of Arjuna. For 10 points, name this god who teaches in the Bhagavad Gita.

This text is a 700-verse section of the Mahabharata in which the warrior Arjuna receives advice from his charioteer on the battlefield of Kurukshetra. It discusses duty, devotion, and action. For 10 points, name this Hindu scripture, whose name means the Song of God.

These are the oldest sacred texts of Hinduism, composed in Sanskrit and made up of four collections, including the Rigveda. They contain hymns, rituals, and philosophical ideas. For 10 points, name these ancient scriptures, whose name means knowledge.

In Hindu and Buddhist belief, this principle holds that a person's actions have consequences that affect their future, including later lives. Good deeds bring good results and bad deeds bring bad results. For 10 points, name this law of cause and effect whose name means action in Sanskrit.

This belief, shared by Hindus, Buddhists, and Jains, holds that the soul is born again into a new body after death. The cycle continues until a person achieves liberation. For 10 points, name this idea, also called rebirth or samsara.

Hindus believe bathing in this river washes away sins. Millions gather on its banks at Varanasi and at the Kumbh Mela. Ashes of the dead are often scattered in it. For 10 points, name this holy river of India.

The Buddha's first sermon laid out four truths, beginning with the idea that life involves suffering. It ties suffering to craving and states that it can end by following a path. For 10 points, name this set of core Buddhist teachings, whose number is in the name.

This path to ending suffering in Buddhism has eight parts: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. For 10 points, name this set of practices that is the fourth of the Four Noble Truths.

In Buddhism, this is the state of freedom from suffering and the cycle of rebirth. The word means blowing out, like a flame going out. For 10 points, name this goal of the Buddhist path, which is the final release.

The Buddha is said to have gained enlightenment while meditating beneath this tree at Bodh Gaya. A descendant of the original still stands there today. For 10 points, name this tree sacred to Buddhists, a type of fig.

Tibetan Buddhists believe this title holder is the reincarnation of a compassionate bodhisattva. The current holder fled Tibet in 1959 and lives in exile in India. For 10 points, give this title of the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism.

This school of Buddhism, which spread from China to Japan, emphasizes meditation rather than study of scriptures. It is known for riddles called koans and for rock gardens in temples. For 10 points, name this form of Buddhism.

This Chinese philosopher is the traditional author of the Tao Te Ching. His name means old master, and legend says he wrote the book before leaving China on a water buffalo. For 10 points, name this founder of Taoism.

This short text of about 81 chapters is the central book of Taoism. It teaches that one should live in harmony with a natural force called the Way, and it praises simplicity and humility. For 10 points, name this classic whose title means the Way and its Power.

This symbol of a circle divided into black and white halves, each with a dot of the other color, represents balance in Taoism. The two halves are opposites that depend on each other. For 10 points, name this Chinese symbol, called taijitu.

This Chinese thinker taught that society works best when people respect their parents, elders, and rulers. He lived around 500 BC, and his ideas became the basis of an ethical system in East Asia. For 10 points, name this philosopher.

This collection of sayings and short dialogues of Confucius and his disciples was compiled by his followers after his death. It begins with the line: is it not a pleasure to learn and to practice what is learned? For 10 points, name this central Confucian text.

This indigenous religion of Japan honors spirits called kami and has shrines at places of natural beauty. Its rituals emphasize purity, and many Japanese couples hold weddings at its shrines. For 10 points, name this religion that, unlike Buddhism, originated in Japan.

This red gate marks the entrance to a Shinto shrine and is a boundary between the ordinary world and sacred space. A famous one stands in the water at Itsukushima Shrine on Miyajima. For 10 points, name this type of Japanese gateway.

This ancient Sanskrit epic tells of a prince exiled to a forest with his wife Sita and his brother Lakshmana. Sita is kidnapped by the demon king Ravana, and the monkey Hanuman helps rescue her. For 10 points, name this epic attributed to the poet Valmiki.
This Hindu goddess of wealth and good fortune is the wife of Vishnu. She is often shown seated on a lotus and holding gold coins. Many people honor her at Diwali. For 10 points, name this goddess.

This Sanskrit syllable is considered the sacred sound of the universe in Hinduism and is also used in Buddhism and Jainism. It is chanted at the beginning of prayers and meditation and is often written in a special symbol. For 10 points, name this mantra.

This largest religion of India has no single founder and no single scripture. Its followers worship many forms of one ultimate reality, called Brahman, including Vishnu, Shiva, and Devi. For 10 points, name this religion, followed by about a billion people, which includes the practice of yoga.

This dome-shaped Buddhist monument holds relics of the Buddha or of revered monks. Pilgrims walk around it clockwise as a form of devotion. A famous example stands at Sanchi in India, and the form influenced the pagoda. For 10 points, name this type of structure, called a chorten in Tibet.

text: This religion was founded in the Punjab region around 1500. Its followers worship one God, reject caste distinctions, and keep their hair uncut under a turban. Their temples are called gurdwaras, where free communal meals are served. For 10 points, name this religion whose scripture is the Guru Granth Sahib.

This man was the first of the ten Sikh gurus. Born in the Punjab in 1469, he taught that there is one God and that all people are equal. He traveled widely, spreading his message through songs and poems. For 10 points, name this founder of Sikhism.

This gold-covered Sikh house of worship in Amritsar sits in the middle of a sacred pool. Visitors cover their heads and remove their shoes before entering, and the Guru Granth Sahib is read inside around the clock. For 10 points, name this shrine, also called Harmandir Sahib.

Sikhs treat this holy book as their living guru. Compiled by Guru Arjan and later expanded by Guru Gobind Singh, it contains hymns by Sikh gurus and by saints of other traditions. For 10 points, name this scripture, which is kept on a throne in every gurdwara.

Guru Gobind Singh created this order of initiated Sikhs in 1699 at Anandpur. Members are expected to wear the five articles of faith and to follow a code of conduct. For 10 points, give this term for the Sikh community of the pure.

These are five items observed by initiated Sikhs, each beginning with the same letter in Punjabi: uncut hair, a comb, a steel bracelet, a short sword, and special undergarments. For 10 points, give the name by which this group of five articles of faith is known.

This ancient Indian religion teaches nonviolence toward all living things. Its monks sometimes sweep the ground before them and wear cloths over their mouths to avoid harming small creatures. It has twenty-four teachers called tirthankaras. For 10 points, name this religion, found mostly in India.

This man, a contemporary of the Buddha, is considered the twenty-fourth and last tirthankara of Jainism. He gave up royal life, wandered as an ascetic, and taught the importance of nonviolence. For 10 points, name this teacher whose name means great hero.
This word, meaning nonviolence, is a basic principle of Jainism, Buddhism, and Hinduism. Mahatma Gandhi made it a central part of his philosophy of resistance. For 10 points, give this Sanskrit term.

Founded in nineteenth-century Persia, this religion teaches the unity of all religions and all humanity. Its followers consider Baha'u'llah to be its prophet. Its houses of worship have nine sides and are open to all faiths. For 10 points, name this religion.

This ancient Persian religion is named for a prophet who taught that the world is a struggle between truth and falsehood. Its followers keep sacred fires burning in their temples. It was the main religion of the Persian Empire. For 10 points, name this faith, which has about a hundred thousand followers worldwide, many of them called Parsis in India.

This Persian prophet is said to have received a vision from the supreme god and wrote hymns called the Gathas. He lived in ancient Iran thousands of years ago, and his teachings emphasize good thoughts, good words, and good deeds. For 10 points, name this founder of a religion that bears his name.

This is the supreme god of Zoroastrianism, whose name means wise lord. He is opposed by the destructive spirit Angra Mainyu, and the prophet Zoroaster is said to have received revelations from him. For 10 points, name this creator god.

This Jamaican-born religious movement considers Haile Selassie, the emperor of Ethiopia, to be a divine figure. Its members often wear dreadlocks and avoid certain foods, and reggae music is associated with it. For 10 points, name this movement, whose followers use the colors red, gold, and green.

This modern nature religion honors a goddess and a horned god and celebrates festivals that mark the turning of the seasons. Many of its practitioners call themselves witches. For 10 points, name this religion associated with Gerald Gardner.

These priests of the ancient Celts served as judges, teachers, and religious leaders. According to Roman writers, they conducted rites in sacred oak groves and cut mistletoe with a golden sickle. For 10 points, name this class of priests.

In Egyptian myth, this god of the dead and the underworld was killed by his brother Set. His wife Isis revived him, and he judged souls in the afterlife. He is often shown green or black, wrapped like a mummy. For 10 points, name this Egyptian god.

This Egyptian sun god sailed across the sky each day in a boat and traveled through the underworld at night. He was often depicted as a man with the head of a falcon and a sun disk. For 10 points, name this chief god of ancient Egypt.

This Egyptian god with a jackal head guided the dead and oversaw mummification. He weighed the hearts of the dead against the feather of truth, and the god Thoth recorded the result. For 10 points, name this deity.
This king of the Greek gods wielded thunderbolts and ruled from Mount Olympus. He was the son of Cronus and Rhea, and his wife was Hera. For 10 points, name this god, called Jupiter by the Romans.

This one-eyed Norse god, ruler of Asgard, gave up an eye in return for wisdom. He rides an eight-legged horse named Sleipnir, and his ravens Huginn and Muninn bring him news. For 10 points, name this chief god of Norse mythology.

This Norse god of thunder wields the hammer Mjolnir and rides a chariot pulled by goats. He fights giants and the serpent Jormungandr. For 10 points, name this god, after whom a day of the week is named.

In Norse belief, brave warriors who die in battle are taken to this hall in Asgard. They fight each day and feast each night, preparing for Ragnarok. For 10 points, name this hall presided over by Odin.

This feathered serpent god of the Aztecs was associated with the wind, learning, and the morning star. Some stories say the Aztec ruler Moctezuma thought Hernan Cortes might be this figure returned. For 10 points, name this deity, called Kukulkan by the Maya.
This belief, found in many indigenous cultures, holds that animals, plants, rivers, and mountains have spirits. The word comes from the Latin for soul. For 10 points, name this type of belief system.

This religion of Haiti combines West African beliefs with elements of Catholicism. Its practitioners honor spirits called lwa and hold ceremonies led by priests called houngans. For 10 points, name this religion, which is often misrepresented in films.

This looped Egyptian symbol resembles a cross with a handle and means life. Many Egyptian gods and pharaohs are shown holding one, and it often appears in tomb paintings and jewelry. For 10 points, name this symbol.

Each year on November 1 and 2, families in Mexico build altars with marigolds, candles, and sugar skulls to honor dead relatives. It blends indigenous traditions with the Catholic holidays of All Saints and All Souls. For 10 points, name this holiday, called Dia de los Muertos in Spanish.

This kind of religious practitioner, found in Siberia, Korea, and many other cultures, is believed to enter a trance and communicate with the spirit world. The word is Evenki in origin. For 10 points, name this type of healer and spiritual intermediary.

This ancient circle of standing stones on Salisbury Plain in England may have been used for religious ceremonies. Many people gather there at the summer solstice, when the sun rises over the Heel Stone. For 10 points, name this prehistoric monument.
